An Herbalist’s SHTF Natural Pharmacy Guide 
50 
Muscle Pain Relief Peppermint: 4, Rosemary: 4, Lavender: 2 
Respiratory Support Eucalyptus: 5, Peppermint: 3, Tea Tree: 2 
Mood Enhancement Grapefruit: 3, Bergamot: 2, Lavender: 3, Ylang Ylang: 2 
Aphrodisiac Ylang Ylang: 3, Sandalwood: 2, Jasmine: 2, Patchouli: 1 
Meditation Frankincense: 3, Sandalwood: 2, Lavender: 1, Clary Sage: 1 
Aromatherapy Sprays 
Aromatherapy sprays offer many benefits for both mind 
and body. To use aromatherapy sprays effectively, simply 
shake the bottle before each use to ensure the oils are 
properly mixed with the solvent. Then, close your eyes and 
spray the mist around your body, room, or onto linens to 
enjoy the benefits of the essential oils.  
Remember to test the spray on a small area first to check 
for any skin sensitivity or allergies before using it more 
extensively. Avoid contact with eyes and keep out of reach 
of children. Citrus oils can increase sun sensitivity so avoid 
direct sunlight on skin where applied.  
To make an aromatherapy spray you can use: 
1. 1 cup water (distilled is best but filtered will work). 
2. 1/2 cup of rubbing alcohol or unscented witch hazel (alcohol helps to keep the mixture for 
longer and witch hazel helps to fix the aroma of the oils). 
3. Put the solution into a spray bottle and add 30- 40 drops of essential oil. Follow the recipes 
below to create your aromatherapy spray blends. 
4. Shake well before use. 
Calming Aromatherapy Spray 
This blend reduces stress and promotes relaxation. Lavender and chamomile soothe, while ylang 
ylang elevates mood and reduces tension. Spray on pillows and linens before bedtime to promote 
restful sleep. 
20 drops Lavender

Aromatherapy Sprays 
Aromatherapy sprays offer many benefits for both mind 
and body. To use aromatherapy sprays effectively, simply 
shake the bottle before each use to ensure the oils are 
properly mixed with the solvent. Then, close your eyes and 
spray the mist around your body, room, or onto linens to 
enjoy the benefits of the essential oils.  
Remember to test the spray on a small area first to check 
for any skin sensitivity or allergies before using it more 
extensively. Avoid contact with eyes and keep out of reach 
of children. Citrus oils can increase sun sensitivity so avoid 
direct sunlight on skin where applied.  
To make an aromatherapy spray you can use: 
1. 1 cup water (distilled is best but filtered will work). 
2. 1/2 cup of rubbing alcohol or unscented witch hazel (alcohol helps to keep the mixture for 
longer and witch hazel helps to fix the aroma of the oils). 
3. Put the solution into a spray bottle and add 30- 40 drops of essential oil. Follow the recipes 
below to create your aromatherapy spray blends. 
4. Shake well before use. 
Calming Aromatherapy Spray 
This blend reduces stress and promotes relaxation. Lavender and chamomile soothe, while ylang 
ylang elevates mood and reduces tension. Spray on pillows and linens before bedtime to promote 
restful sleep. 
20 drops Lavender

An Herbalist’s SHTF Natural Pharmacy Guide 
52 
Steam Inhalation 
Steam inhalation offers soothing relief for sore throats, coughs and 
irritated airways. They can ease breathing during colds, allergies or 
respiratory infections, and aid in sinus and nasal decongestion. They 
help moisturize dry airways, loosen mucus for e asier expulsion, 
provide sinus relief by clearing congestion, and can help reduce 
inflammation in the airways. Do not use steam inhalations for 
children under 6 years old. 
To make a steam inhalation using essential oils, follow these 
simple steps: 
1. Boil water in a kettle or pot. 
2. Fill a large heatproof bowl with the hot water. Allow the water to cool slightly to avoid burns. 
3. Add 4-5 drops of your chosen essential oil to the hot water. 
4. Place the bowl on a stable surface where you can lean over it comfortably. 
5. Lower your face over the bowl but not too close to avoid burns. 
6. Cover your head and the bowl with a towel to create a tent-like effect that traps the steam. 
7. Close your eyes and inhale deeply for about 5-10 minutes. 
8. Be cautious as the steam can be hot, so take breaks if needed. 
9. Drink water when you have finished to rehydrate.  
10. Repeat twice a day or as needed. 
Blends for steam inhalation: 
• 2 drops Eucalyptus oil, 2 drops Tea Tree oil and 1 drop Thyme oil 
• 2 drops Peppermint oil, 2 drops Eucalyptus, 1 drop Lemon oil 
• 2 drops Peppermint, 2 drops Thyme oil, 1 drop Tea Tree oil

An Herbalist’s SHTF Natural Pharmacy Guide 
52 
Steam Inhalation 
Steam inhalation offers soothing relief for sore throats, coughs and 
irritated airways. They can ease breathing during colds, allergies or 
respiratory infections, and aid in sinus and nasal decongestion. They 
help moisturize dry airways, loosen mucus for e asier expulsion, 
provide sinus relief by clearing congestion, and can help reduce 
inflammation in the airways. Do not use steam inhalations for 
children under 6 years old. 
To make a steam inhalation using essential oils, follow these 
simple steps: 
1. Boil water in a kettle or pot. 
2. Fill a large heatproof bowl with the hot water. Allow the water to cool slightly to avoid burns. 
3. Add 4-5 drops of your chosen essential oil to the hot water. 
4. Place the bowl on a stable surface where you can lean over it comfortably. 
5. Lower your face over the bowl but not too close to avoid burns. 
6. Cover your head and the bowl with a towel to create a tent-like effect that traps the steam. 
7. Close your eyes and inhale deeply for about 5-10 minutes. 
8. Be cautious as the steam can be hot, so take breaks if needed. 
9. Drink water when you have finished to rehydrate.  
10. Repeat twice a day or as needed. 
Blends for steam inhalation: 
• 2 drops Eucalyptus oil, 2 drops Tea Tree oil and 1 drop Thyme oil 
• 2 drops Peppermint oil, 2 drops Eucalyptus, 1 drop Lemon oil 
• 2 drops Peppermint, 2 drops Thyme oil, 1 drop Tea Tree oil

An Herbalist’s SHTF Natural Pharmacy Guide 
53 
Chest Rub 
This is a simple recipe to make a chest rub for adults 
with respiratory issues. It reduces coughing, and 
provides comfort during colds, flu and respiratory 
problems. Do not apply to broken skin or near the 
eyes.  
Ingredients: 
• 2 tablespoons coconut oil 
• 10 drops Eucalyptus 
• 5 drops Peppermint  
• 5 drops Thyme  
Instructions: 
Melt the coconut oil and mix in the essential oils. Store in a small, sterilized pot with a lid. Allow the 
mixture to cool and solidify before use. Apply to the chest and back a few times a day to relieve 
congestion. This chest rub can be especially useful at night when symptoms often worsen and can 
affect sleep quality. 
Rose Hydrosol  
A hydrosol, also known as floral water, is a byproduct of the steam distillation process used to extract 
essential oils from plants. During distillation, steam passes through plant material, vaporizing the 
volatile compounds. These vapors then condense back into liquid form. The resulting liquid separates 
into two parts: essential oil and hydrosol. While essential oils are highly concentrated, hydrosols 
contain the water-soluble compounds of the plant along with tiny amounts of essential oil.  
Rose hydrosol offers numerous benefits, making it a versatile 
addition to your skincare routine. It acts as a natural toner, 
hydrating and balancing the skin's pH while reducing redness, 
irritation, and inflammation. Rich in antioxidants, it protects the 
skin from free radical damage and premature aging. As a natural 
astringent, it tightens pores and promotes a smoother complexion 
without the harshness of alcohol -based astringents. The soothing 
scent of roses provides aromatherapeutic benefits, reducing stress 
and promoting relaxation. Additionally, rose hydrosol can cool and refresh the skin, making it perfect 
for hot weather or after sun exposure. It can also be used as a hair mist to hydrate the scalp, reduce 
dandruff, and add a subtle fragrance to the hair. Furthermore, it can be used as a natural makeup 
setting spray to keep your makeup looking fresh and dewy, and it serves various other purposes, 
such as in DIY beauty recipes, as a linen spray, or to freshen up a room. 
The shelf life of rose hydrosol is typically around 6 months when stored properly. To maximize its 
shelf life, it should be kept in a clean, airtight glass container and stored in a cool, dark place, such 
as a refrigerator. Storing it away from direct sunlight and heat sources will help maintain its quality 
and potency for a longer period. If you notice any changes in smell, color, or consistency, it is best 
to discard it and prepare a fresh batch.

An Herbalist’s SHTF Natural Pharmacy Guide 
54 
Supplies Needed: 
• 3 cups fresh rose petals, rinsed and cleaned 
• Wide pot or saucepan 
• Small heat-proof bowl (you may need 2 bowls, one to raise up the other to make sure it is 
higher than the water level) 
• Ice cubes 
• Freezer or zip lock bag 
• 1800 ml distilled water 
• Cheesecloth 
• Sterilized spray bottles 
Instructions: 
1. Place a small heat-resistant bowl in the center of 
a wide pot. (If the bowl is lower than the water 
level then invert another bowl below it as a stand 
and put the collection bowl on top of it to raise it 
up). 
2. Add the washed rose petals to the pot, ensuring 
they don't get trapped under the bowl. 
3. Pour distilled water into the pot until the rose 
petals are just submerged. You may not need all 
the water. 
4. Invert the pot lid and place it on top of the pot. Add ice cubes into the freezer bag and put 
on top of the inverted lid. 
5. Bring the water to a boil. 
6. Empty the bag of ice as it melts and refill with more ice. 
7. Reduce the heat to low and let it simmer for 30–45 minutes. 
8. Carefully remove the lid to check the color of the rose petals. Once they have lost their color, 
the process is complete. 
9. Allow the rose water to cool completely. 
10. Transfer the cooled rose water from the bowl into a spray bottle. 
11. Refrigerate and use for up to 6 months. 
12. The water in the pan is rose water and can also be utilized. Strain through a cheesecloth and 
put into another clean sterilized bottle. 
The rose water left from the distillation process can be used in a variety of ways like the hydrosol. It 
can be added to baths for a relaxing and aromatic experience or used as a hair rinse to add shine 
and a subtle rose scent. The rose water can also be incorporated into homemade beauty products, 
such as face masks, lotions, and creams, or used in culinary recipes to add a floral flavor to dishes 
and beverages.

An Herbalist’s SHTF Natural Pharmacy Guide 
55 
Lip Balm 
Ingredients: 
• 2 tablespoons of beeswax pellets 
• 2 tablespoons of shea butter or cocoa butter 
• 2 tablespoons of coconut oil 
• 10-15 drops of essential oil (such as peppermint, 
lavender, or vanilla) 
• 1/2 teaspoon of vitamin E oil (optional, for added 
nourishment) 
Instructions: 
1. In a double boiler, melt the beeswax pellets, shea butter (or cocoa butter), and coconut oil 
over low heat. Stir occasionally until fully melted and well combined. 
2. Once melted, remove the mixture from heat and add the vitamin E oil if using. Stir well to 
incorporate. 
3. Add 20 drops of your chosen essential oil to the mixture. Stir thoroughly to ensure the 
essential oil is evenly distributed. 
4. Carefully pour the melted mixture into your lip balm containers. These can be small tubes of 
pots. Make sure they are sterilized. Use a small funnel or a pipette if needed to avoid spills. 
5. Allow the lip balm to cool and harden at room temperature.  
You can customize the recipe by using different carrier oils, such as almond oil or jojoba oil, or by 
blending multiple essential oils for a unique scent. Avoid citrus oils as they can cause burns when 
exposed to sunlight. Store your lip balm in a cool, dr y place. It should last for several months, 
depending on the freshness of the ingredients used. Ensure all tools and containers are clean and 
dry before use to maintain the quality and safety of your lip balm. Don't forget the patch test before 
use. 
Anti-Aging Face Oil 
This oil reduces the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles, 
promotes skin elasticity, improves overall skin tone whilst 
soothing and calming the skin. This oil can be used twice a day 
as part of your daily routine. Not recommended for oily skin. 
The Vitamin E oil helps to conserve the oil for longer increasing 
its shelf life whilst providing nourishing skin benefits. The oil 
should keep for at least a year depending on the freshness of 
your ingredients. 
Ingredients: 
• 2 tablespoons Jojoba oil 
• 8 drops Rose

An Herbalist’s SHTF Natural Pharmacy Guide 
57 
Chapter 5: Tinctures 
Making and using tinctures offer numerous benefits, both 
practical and therapeutic. Tinctures provide a concentrated 
and potent form of herbal medicine, making it easy to 
incorporate the healing properties of plants into daily life. 
They are highly effecti ve, with a long shelf life and 
convenient dosage forms, often requiring just a few drops. 
The alcohol base of tinctures effectively extracts and 
preserves the medicinal compounds of herbs, ensuring a 
high level of efficacy. Making tinctures at home allows for 
customization, enabling individuals to tailor blends to their 
specific health needs and preferences. Homemade tinctures are often more cost-effective compared 
to store-bought alternatives. 
Ingredients: 
• 1 cup dried herbs or 2 cups fresh herbs  
• 2 cups vodka (at least 80 proof) 
Materials: 
• Clean glass jar with a tight-fitting lid 
• Cheesecloth 
• Sterilized dark glass dropper bottles 
Instructions: 
1. If using  fresh herbs, rinse them thoroughly and pat dry. Chop them finely to increase the 
surface area for extraction. 
2. If using dried herbs or roots ensure they are clean and free from any debris. Make sure they 
are broken up, finely chopped or ground. 
3. Place the herbs into the clean glass jar. 
4. Pour the vodka over the herbs until they are completely covered. The vodka should be about 
1-2 inches above the herbs. 
5. Seal the jar tightly with the lid. 
6. Label the jar with the date and the type of herbs used. 
7. Store the jar in a cool, dark place (like a pantry or cupboard) for 4 -6 weeks. Shake the jar 
gently every few days to help with the extraction process. 
8. Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh strainer or cheesecloth into a clean bowl, squeezing 
out as much liquid as possible from the herbs. 
9. Pour the strained tincture into a clean, labeled glass dropper bottle. Properly stored tinctures 
can last for several years.

An Herbalist’s SHTF Natural Pharmacy Guide 
58 
Dosage: 
Tincture dosages can vary depending on the herb and the individual's needs. A common dosage is 
1-2 dropperfuls (approximately 20-40 drops), taken 1-3 times daily. A more precise dosage is 1-3 
drops per kilo of your weight divided into 2 -3 doses per day. 1 -2 times your weight is usually 
enough in drops. 3 times your weight would be in very severe cases. Dilute in a small amount of 
water and take at least a 1-hour interval from eating or drinking anything other than water to increase 
absorbency. 
Always research the specific herb you are using to understand its effects, potential side effects, and 
interactions with medications. 
Follow the basic tincture preparation method using the following measurements in these recipes 
to add these tinctures to your home herbal pharmacy:  
Feminine Balance Tincture 
This tincture recipe can be used to manage menopause and 
menstrual symptoms and to balance cycles.  
Ingredients 
• 1/3 cup Black Cohosh root  
• 1/3 cup Dong Quai root 
• 1/3 cup Red Raspberry leaf 
• 2 cups Vodka (80-100 proof) 
The tinctures can also be prepared separately using 1 cup of  each plant and 2 cups of  vodka in 
separate containers and then you can combine them into your dropper bottle. This goes for all the 
following tincture recipes.  
Precautions 
Avoid using this tincture during pregnancy and breastfeeding. Also avoid this tincture if you have 
hormonal conditions such as hormone -sensitive cancers or endometriosis. Discontinue use if you 
experience any allergic reactions. 
Immune System Tincture 
Perfect to speed recovery from colds, viruses, flus and infections.  
Ingredients: 
• 1/3 cup Echinacea  
• 1/3 cup Elderberry 
• 1/3 cup Astragalus root 
• 2 cups Vodka (80-100 proof)

An Herbalist’s SHTF Natural Pharmacy Guide 
59 
Precautions: 
Avoid using this tincture if you have autoimmune diseases, during pregnancy and breastfeeding. 
Discontinue use if you experience any allergic reactions. Echinacea should not be used continuously 
for more than 8 weeks. Take breaks between courses. 
Vitality Tincture 
Use daily to enhance energy, reduce stress, and support overall 
vitality. Perfect for an instant pick-me-up. 
Ingredients: 
• 1/3 cup American Ginseng root 
• 1/3 cup Ashwagandha root 
• 1/3 cup Rhodiola root 
• 2 cups Vodka (80-100 proof) 
Precautions: 
Avoid using this tincture during pregnancy and breastfeeding, if taking hormonal medications or if 
you have autoimmune conditions. This tincture may interact with sedatives, thyroid medications, and 
blood pressure medications. 
Allergy and Respiratory System Tincture 
This tincture works well to alleviate allergy symptoms and support respiratory health. It can be used 
for asthma, bronchitis and coughs. 
Ingredients: 
• 1/3 cup Thyme 
• 1/3 cup Nettle 
• 1/3 cup Mullein leaf 
• 2 cups Vodka (80-100 proof) 
Precautions: 
Avoid this tincture during pregnancy and breastfeeding. Those with blood pressure issues or on 
blood pressure medications should use the tincture cautiously, as it may affect blood pressure levels. 
Diabetics or individuals on blood sugar-lowering medications should monitor their levels closely, as 
the tincture may impact blood sugar. It should be avoided by those with kidney conditions or on 
diuretic medications. If allergic reactions occur, discontinue use.

An Herbalist’s SHTF Natural Pharmacy Guide 
61 
Chapter 6: Glycerites 
Glycerites are herbal extracts made using glycerin as the 
solvent instead of alcohol, making them an excellent 
alternative for those sensitive to alcohol or for children. 
Glycerin is a sweet, syrupy liquid derived from plants and 
is effective at extracting the medicinal properties of herbs. 
Glycerites are gentle, easy to administer, and have a 
pleasant taste. 
Materials: 
• Clean glass jar with a tight-fitting lid 
• Container for mixing 
• Cheesecloth or fine strainer 
• Sterilized dropper bottles for storage 
• Straw 
Ingredients: 
• Fresh or dried herbs 
• Vegetable glycerin (preferably organic) 
• Distilled water (if using dried herbs) 
Instructions: 
1. For fresh herbs, chop them finely to increase surface area. 
2. For dried herbs, crush or grind them to a coarse powder. 
3. Fill the glass jar halfway with the prepared herbs. 
4. If using dried herbs, combine 3 parts glycerin to 1-part distilled water and pour over the 
herbs. For example, for 800 ml of solution, mix 200 ml of water with 600ml of glycerine. 
Mix the glycerine and water in a separate container before adding to the herbs. Ensure they 
are completely submerged.  
5. For fresh herbs, use undiluted glycerin. 
6. Leave about 1 inch of space at the top of the jar. 
7. Push a strap down into the mixture and stir around to release any air that may be trapped 
beneath the glycerine. 
8. Seal the jar tightly and store it in a cool, dark place. 
9. Shake the jar gently every day to mix the contents. 
10. After 4-6 weeks, strain the mixture through cheesecloth or a fine strainer into a clean bowl, 
squeezing out as much liquid as possible from the herbs. 
11. Pour the strained glycerite into dropper bottles for easy use.

An Herbalist’s SHTF Natural Pharmacy Guide 
63 
Chapter 7: Herb Infused Oils 
Herb-infused oils have a long history of medicinal benefits and versatile uses. These oils, created by 
infusing herbs in carrier oils, offer a natural approach to skincare. Depending on what herbs you 
select they can provide natural pain relief, stress rel ief, hair care, wound healing, and anti -
inflammatory purposes, making them a valuable part of holistic remedies and natural healing 
practices. Dried herbs are best to avoid mold and spoilage. 
Cold Infusion 
1. Fill a clean, dry glass jar with dried herbs and cover them completely with carrier oil (such as 
olive oil, almond oil, or jojoba oil).  
2. Seal the jar and let it sit in a cool dark place for 4-6 weeks, shaking occasionally. 
3. When extraction time is complete strain with a cheesecloth, into a clean glass jar or bottle. 
Squeeze the herbs to extract as much oil as possible. 
4. Label the jar with the date and type of herb-infused oil. 
5. Store in a cool, dark place. Properly stored herb-infused oils can last up to a year. 
Heat Infusion 
1. Place dried herbs in a double boiler or slow 
cooker and cover just enough to submerge with 
carrier oil. Set to low heat.  
2. Maintain a gentle heat ensuring the oil does not 
burn (keep it below 140°F). Strain the oil with a 
cheesecloth after it has cooled.  
3. Heat the plants and oil until the plant material 
becomes crispy to break.  
4. Strain with a cheesecloth, into a clean glass jar 
or bottle. Squeeze the herbs to extract as much 
oil as possible. 
5. Label the jar with the date and type of herb-infused oil. 
6.  
7. Store in a cool, dark place. Properly stored herb-infused oils can last up to a year. 
Now you know how to infuse oil; you can use these methods to prepare the following recipes: 
Rosemary Oil 
Rosemary-infused oil offers a multitude of benefits for both external and internal use. Externally, it 
promotes hair health by stimulating hair growth, improving scalp circulation, and strengthening hair

An Herbalist’s SHTF Natural Pharmacy Guide 
66 
Chapter 8: Herbal Home Extractions 
Cough Syrup 
This cough syrup helps soothe the throat, helps with coughs, boosts the immune system, and reduces 
inflammation. Elderberries and echinacea support immune health, ginger root soothes inflammation, 
and honey provides antimicrobial properties and soothes the throat. 
Ingredients: 
• 1/2 cup dried elderberries 
• 1/2 cup dried echinacea root 
• 1/4 cup grated ginger root 
• 1 cinnamon stick 
• 1 and a 1/2 cups raw honey 
• 4 cups water 
Instructions: 
1. Combine elderberries, echinacea root, ginger root, and cinnamon stick with water in a pot. 
2. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes. 
3. Remove from heat and allow to cool with the lid in place. Strain the mixture and let it cool. 
4. Stir in honey until well combined. 
5. Store in a sterilized glass jar in the refrigerator for up to 2 months. 
6. Take 1 tablespoon as needed for adults or 1 teaspoon for children. 2-3 times per day. 
Precautions: 
Avoid using it for children under 2 years due to the honey. 
Herbal Vinegar 
Herbal-infused vinegars offer a multitude of benefits for topical, culinary, and skincare purposes. 
When used topically, these vinegars can act as natural astringents and cleansing agents for the skin. 
They can also be used as facial toners to tighten pores, balance oil production, and promote a radiant 
complexion. The antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties of herbs infused in vinegar make it 
effective in treating acne, soothing sunburns, and promoting skin health.

2. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes. 
3. Remove from heat and allow to cool with the lid in place. Strain the mixture and let it cool. 
4. Stir in honey until well combined. 
5. Store in a sterilized glass jar in the refrigerator for up to 2 months. 
6. Take 1 tablespoon as needed for adults or 1 teaspoon for children. 2-3 times per day. 
Precautions:

Herbal-infused vinegars offer a multitude of benefits for topical, culinary, and skincare purposes. 
When used topically, these vinegars can act as natural astringents and cleansing agents for the skin. 
They can also be used as facial toners to tighten pores, balance oil production, and promote a radiant 
complexion. The antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties of herbs infused in vinegar make it 
effective in treating acne, soothing sunburns, and promoting skin health.

An Herbalist’s SHTF Natural Pharmacy Guide 
67 
Culinary uses of herbal -infused vinegars add a unique and flavorful 
twist to dishes. They can enhance salads, marinades, dressings, and 
sauces with a burst of herbal essence.  
Herbal-infused vinegars can be used as a natural hair rinse to add 
shine, balance pH levels, and strengthen hair. For hair use it is best to 
use an apple cider vinegar. Rosemary can work well for hair care. 
Thyme vinegar makes a great treatment for athlete's feet due to their 
antimicrobial and antifungal properties.  
Ingredients: 
• 1 cup finely chopped fresh herbs (like thyme or sage) 
• 2 cups organic vinegar of your choice 
Instructions: 
1. Place fresh herbs in a clean glass jar. 
2. Pour vinegar over the herbs, ensuring they are fully submerged. 
3. Seal the jar and store in a cool, dark place for 2-4 weeks, shaking occasionally. 
4. Strain the vinegar and store it in a clean glass bottle. 
5. Use as desired. 
6. Dilute before applying to the skin or hair with 4 parts water to 1-part  vinegar to avoid 
irritation. 
Herbal Wine 
Herbal wine combines the relaxing properties of wine with the medicinal benefits of herbs, offering 
a unique way to enjoy herbal remedies. 
Ingredients: 
• 1 cup fresh herbs (e.g., lemon balm, sage, ginseng) 
• 1 bottle white or red wine 
Instructions: 
1. Place fresh herbs in a clean glass jar or wine bottle. 
2. Pour wine over the herbs. 
3. Seal the container and store in a cool, dark place 
for 1-2 weeks, shaking occasionally. 
4. Strain the wine and store it in a clean bottle. 
5. Enjoy in moderation. A small cup at the end of a 
day is sufficient.

Chapter 9: More Herbal Skin Care Recipes 
Deodorant Recipe 
This natural deodorant helps to neutralize odor and absorb 
moisture without the use of harmful chemicals. It has 
antimicrobial properties which help to eliminate stinky 
bacteria. 
Ingredients: 
• 2 tablespoons shea butter 
• 3 tablespoons coconut oil 
• 3 tablespoons baking soda 
• 2 tablespoons arrowroot powder (or organic cornstarch, optional) 
• 30 drops of essential oils (lavender, tea tree, sage and lemon are great options for deodorant) 
Instructions: 
1. Melt the coconut oil in a double boiler. 
2. Remove from heat and stir in baking soda and arrowroot powder until well combined. 
3. Add essential oils and mix thoroughly. 
4. Pour into a clean container and allow to cool and solidify. 
5. Apply a small amount to underarms as needed. 
Precautions: 
Perform a patch test to ensure no skin irritation. Avoid use on broken or irritated skin. 
Natural Repellent 
This natural repellent recipe not only helps protect against 
insect bites but also avoids the use of synthetic chemicals 
commonly found in commercial repellents, making it a safer 
alternative for both the environment and the user. 
Ingredients: 
• 1/2 cup fresh rosemary sprigs 
• 1/4 cup whole cloves 
• 10 drops citronella essential oil 
• 1 cup rubbing alcohol (isopropyl alcohol)

Instructions: 
1. Wash the fresh rosemary sprigs thoroughly and pat them dry. 
2. Place the rosemary sprigs and whole cloves into a clean glass jar. 
3. Pour the rubbing alcohol over the herbs, ensuring they are completely submerged. 
4. Seal the jar tightly with a lid. 
5. Store the jar in a cool, dark place for 1-2 weeks, shaking it gently every few days to mix the 
contents. 
6. After the infusion period, strain the liquid through cheesecloth or a fine mesh strainer into a 
clean glass spray bottle. 
7. Add the citronella essential oil to the mixture. 
8. Shake the bottle well before each use.  
9. Reapply as needed, especially after sweating or exposure to water. 
Precautions: 
Perform a patch test on a small area of skin before applying it more broadly to check for any allergic 
reactions or skin sensitivity. Avoid spraying the repellent directly onto the face; instead, spray it onto 
your hands and then apply to the face, keeping  it away from the eyes and mouth. Due to the high 
flammability of rubbing alcohol, keep the repellent away from open flames and sources of heat. When 
using on children, apply cautiously and avoid their hands to prevent accidental contact with their 
eyes. Be careful not to spray onto clothing as it may stain. 
Natural Sunscreen Recipe 
This natural sunscreen provides protection against UV rays 
without the use of synthetic chemicals. Zinc oxide acts as a 
physical barrier to block UV rays. Carrot seed essential oil, cold 
pressed raspberry seed oil , and coconut oil all have SPF 
protection. 
Ingredients: 
• 1/4 cup coconut oil 
• 1/4 cup cold pressed raspberry seed oil 
• 1/4 cup shea butter 
• 1/4 cup beeswax 
• 2 tablespoons non-nano zinc oxide 
• 10-15 drops carrot seed essential oil 
Instructions: 
1. Melt coconut oil, shea butter, and beeswax in a double boiler.  
2. Add in the raspberry seed oil. 
3. Remove from the heat and stir in zinc oxide carefully.

Natural Toothpaste Recipe 
This natural toothpaste harnesses the benefits of 
several key ingredients for maintaining oral health. 
Coconut oil has antibacterial properties that help 
reduce harmful bacteria in the mouth and promote 
overall oral hygiene. Baking soda acts as a gentle 
abrasive, effectively cleaning and whitening teeth 
without damaging enamel. Bentonite clay, if used, 
helps to detoxify and remineralize teeth due to its high 
mineral content. Peppermint essential oil not only 
provides a refreshing taste but also has antimicrobial properties that can help reduce oral bacteria 
and freshen breath. Sea salt adds an extra cleaning boost by providing natural minerals that can aid 
in strengthening teeth, while stevia powder offers a pleasant sweetness without the negative effects 
of sugar. 
Ingredients: 
• 1/2 cup coconut oil 
• 2-3 tablespoons baking soda 
• 1-2 tablespoons bentonite clay  
• 10-15 drops peppermint essential oil (or another essential oil of your choice, such as 
spearmint or cinnamon) 
• 1 teaspoon stevia powder (optional, for sweetness) 
• 1/2 teaspoon fine sea salt (optional) 
Instructions: 
1. If the coconut oil is solid, melt it by placing the jar in warm water or using a double boiler. 
2. In a small bowl, combine the coconut oil and baking soda. Mix well to form a smooth paste. 
3. Add the bentonite clay. Avoid using metal utensils with bentonite clay as it can reduce its 
effectiveness. 
4. Add the peppermint essential oil (or your preferred essential oil) and stevia powder, and mix 
thoroughly. 
5. If using sea salt, add it and mix well. 
6. Transfer the mixture to a small glass jar or any airtight container.
